family.tagline: A translator, a sound designer and two children share one Companion Core.
family.story: Meenakshi runs a translation and tutoring agency from the conservatory table, and Ravi designs sound upstairs beside a record player. Arjun, fifteen, plays in the guest bedroom, and Kavya, ten, studies at her desk. One Companion Core sits on a credenza in the living room.

companion.name: Clover
companion.job: Drafts reply messages to Meenakshi’s clients and pupils from her notes.
companion.limits: Writes drafts and nothing more. Meenakshi sends each reply herself.

companion.name: Maple
companion.job: Drafts delivery notes for Ravi’s sound packs from his file lists.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Ravi reads each note and sends it himself.

popup.title: Ravi carries the parcel indoors
popup.body: A parcel waits under the slatted canopy. Ravi carries it past the kitchen and the utility room to the living room, where Kavya clears the credenza.

popup.title: Arjun unpacks the Companion Core
popup.body: The lid lifts: the Companion Core, a power cable, a guide and a recovery USB drive. Arjun carries the Core to the credenza.

popup.title: Ravi plugs in, Kavya presses
popup.body: Ravi plugs in the cable, and Kavya presses the power button. The Core wakes and opens a Wi-Fi network of its own.

popup.title: Meenakshi joins on her phone
popup.body: Meenakshi opens the Wi-Fi settings on her phone and joins the Core’s own network. Then she picks the home network.

popup.title: Meenakshi picks the first agent
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Meenakshi picks Hermes, and the family adds ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors and LibreTranslate. Then the family walks away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Clover says hello
popup.body: Meenakshi messages the agent she named Clover from the sofa. Clover answers from the Core on the credenza.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: meenakshi
say.text: Hello, Meenakshi. I am Clover. Where shall we begin?

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Ravi finds the song Kavya hummed
popup.body: On the chesterfield, Ravi finds the song Kavya hummed at breakfast. Navidrome serves his own music files from the Core to the phone in his hand.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: The brochure gets a first pass
popup.body: A client’s brochure arrives in Spanish. Meenakshi runs a first pass in LibreTranslate, then polishes it herself. The models were downloaded once, so the Core does the translating.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Meenakshi moves a lesson
popup.body: By the fireplace, Meenakshi names two free slots for a pupil’s parent. Clover drafts the reply on the Core’s local model, and Meenakshi reads it and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: meenakshi
say.text: Here is a draft with both slots. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for notes, shopping, chores and expenses

popup.title: Arjun clears, then ticks it off
popup.body: After breakfast it is Arjun’s turn to clear the table. He ticks the chore off in HomeHub, and the family’s chore list is served from the Core.

beats.capability: write documents, spreadsheets and slides with a full office suite in your browser

popup.title: Meenakshi lays out a bilingual contract
popup.body: Two languages, two columns. Meenakshi lays out a client’s contract in ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors, which runs on the Core and shows in her browser.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: The old glossary is still there
popup.body: A client returns after a year. Meenakshi opens the old folder in Nextcloud. The glossary she built is saved on the Core, not in a rented drive.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for notes, shopping, chores and expenses

popup.title: Kavya adds tamarind to the list
popup.body: At the fridge, Kavya sees the tamarind is nearly gone and adds it to the HomeHub list. Meenakshi reads the list, served from the Core, before she shops.

beats.capability: send a push notification to your phone from any script or automation with one request

popup.title: Ravi sends the lunch bell
popup.body: At the range, Ravi runs a one-line script that sends ‘lunch’ to the family’s phones through ntfy. The ntfy server that delivers it runs on the Core.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: Arjun’s game runs downstairs
popup.body: Saturday afternoon, Arjun opens his Steam library in a browser on the bed. Steam Headless runs the session on the Core downstairs.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host

popup.title: Arjun’s game password joins the vault
popup.body: Arjun keeps forgetting his Valve password. He saves it in the family’s VaultWarden vault, which works with the Bitwarden apps and lives on the Core.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Arjun backs up a painting
popup.body: On his bed, Arjun looks over the pictures he took of Kavya’s finished painting. Over the home network, his phone backs them up to Immich on the Core.

beats.capability: run a quiz night for a small group on your own Core

popup.title: Kavya and Arjun settle it
popup.body: Kavya and Arjun argue over who knows more. She sets questions in Razzia, and he answers from his own device, with the Core serving the quiz.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Kavya labels her frog painting
popup.body: By the easel, Kavya types frog into LibreTranslate and letters the Spanish word, rana, under her painting. Its language models were downloaded once, so the translating happens at home.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Kavya keeps a reading journal
popup.body: After school, Kavya adds a line about her library book to her Obsidian journal. It is a plain Markdown note on the Core, readable in any text editor.

beats.capability: edit audio in a browser tab

popup.title: Ravi trims a record he copied
popup.body: Beside the record player, Ravi trims a record he copied to files. The Core serves AudioMass, and the trimming happens in his browser tab.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: Ravi fits the recording week
popup.body: On Monday morning, Ravi fits the week’s recording hours into Companion Planning, one local file on the Core. He leaves Thursday afternoon empty for retakes.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Maple drafts the delivery note
popup.body: A studio is waiting for a pack of door sounds. Ravi lists the files, and Maple drafts the delivery note on the Core’s local model. Ravi sends it himself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: ravi
say.text: The note names the pack and lists the files. Read it, then send it.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Kavya waters, then writes it down
popup.body: After school, Kavya waters the planter by the pool and notes it in HortusFox. The planter’s care history lives on the Core.

popup.title: Four routines share one Companion Core
popup.body: Translation, sound, game sessions and homework run on one Companion Core, under the villa’s dark tile roofs.

closing.body: Your client work, family music and homework can live on a Companion Core at home. Pick your apps in the Companion Hub store.

notes: The house has no TV, no office and no bookshelf. The media beat sits at the couch (Navidrome); Arjun plays in a browser on his bed, never a screen; Meenakshi works at the conservatory trestle table.
Both companions are Hermes. Clover and Maple draft; Meenakshi and Ravi read and send. The Hermes note rides on ftue-hello, table-reschedule and records-delivery.

LibreTranslate beats carry the models-downloaded line and the Core does the work. Spanish appears in two LibreTranslate beats; the listing says dozens of languages and persona-apps uses French as the example.
Steam Headless: Valve account note, no title, no frame rate, home network only. guest-vault names the Valve sign-in but not the app, so no with entry.

ntfy iOS push uses an upstream relay; kitchen-bell says only that the ntfy server runs on the Core. AudioMass exports by browser download, so no file-storage claim. No Companion Memory beat; memory flags are false.
Starts at the Core (living room), then the conservatory beside it, kitchen, upstairs east to west (Arjun, Kavya, Ravi), the pool garden, the street.
kids-tortoise is a Razzia quiz (one manager password set at install, no account per player; no replaces chip). The id is kept so the ads file still points at it.
